claim: Most reported cases of EOPPC are of serous histology (serous surface carcinoma).

evidence.quote: Most cases are of serous histology; however, nonserous tumors have been observed.
evidence.note: States most EOPPC cases are serous histology. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote does not name EOPPC as the disease.

claim: The probability of survival is better for advanced ovarian cancer, for which a median survival of up to 2 years is possible.

evidence.quote: The majority of patients with ovarian cancer present with advanced disease, and in this group of patients, the median survival time is only 3 years.
evidence.note: States median survival of 3 years for advanced disease, a different value than the claimed up to 2 years.

claim: Chemotherapy-induced N&V is one of the most common and distressing acute side effects of cancer treatment.

evidence.quote: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) is one of the most distressing cancer treatment side effects, affecting 20-70% of patients despite routine antiemetic prescription.
evidence.note: States CINV is among the most distressing treatment side effects with 20-70% frequency. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'One of the most common' acute side effect and acute timing not stated.

evidence.quote: Nausea and vomiting are the most common side effects of chemotherapy.
evidence.note: States nausea and vomiting are the most common chemotherapy side effects. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Quote omits 'distressing' and 'acute'; says only most common side effects.

claim: In a review of 1,612 patients referred to an outpatient palliative care center where patients with advanced cancer were seen by both a palliative care nurse and a physician, more than half of patients with moderate to severe pain did not respond to an initial palliative care consultation.

evidence.quote: More than half of the patients with moderate/severe pain were nonresponders, and about one-third of the patients with mild pain had an increase in pain severity to moderate/severe levels at the first follow-up.
evidence.note: Same 1612-patient outpatient palliative care cohort; more than half with moderate/severe pain were nonresponders. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Sample size 1,612 and outpatient palliative care setting not stated.

claim: Methadone is both a mu-receptor agonist and an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist.

evidence.quote: Methadone hydrochloride is a mu-agonist; a synthetic opioid analgesic with multiple actions qualitatively similar to those of morphine, the most prominent of which involve the central nervous system and organs composed of smooth muscle.
evidence.note: Label states methadone is a mu-agonist opioid. Strict re-read: the quote does not state NMDA receptor antagonism not stated.

evidence.quote: Some data also indicate that methadone acts as an antagonist at the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor.
evidence.note: NMDA antagonism stated as "some data indicate"; its clinical contribution is described as unknown.

claim: Pain is one of the most common symptoms in cancer patients and often has a negative impact on patients' functional status and quality of life (QOL).

evidence.quote: Neuropathic cancer pain is experienced by 30-40% of patients with cancer. It significantly reduces quality of life and overall wellbeing for patients living with and beyond cancer.
evidence.note: Gives prevalence and quality-of-life effect for the neuropathic pain subtype only, not all cancer pain.

evidence.quote: One of the biggest problems regarding the treatment of cancer patients is pain, whether due to the cancer or the treatment itself.
evidence.note: Calls pain one of the biggest problems in cancer care; no prevalence or functional status figures.

claim: Studies have shown that following antiemetic protocols that include dexamethasone can improve patient outcomes and reduce the need for rescue medications.

evidence.quote: In patients receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy (MEC), dexamethasone plus a 5HT3RA improved complete CIV control compared to a 5HT3RA alone (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.21-1.39).
evidence.note: Dexamethasone regimen improved vomiting control (outcome), but record states nothing on rescue medication use.

claim: Malnutrition is a common problem in cancer patients that has been recognized as an important component of adverse outcomes, including increased morbidity and mortality and decreased quality of life.

evidence.quote: In adults with cancer, malnutrition was more common than low MM or sarcopenia, although all conditions were associated with a higher mortality risk, regardless of the method of adjusting for MM.
evidence.note: Malnutrition linked to higher mortality risk; morbidity and quality of life not addressed.

evidence.quote: In fact, cancer-associated sarcopenia plays a key role in determining higher rates of morbidity, mortality, treatment-induced toxicities, prolonged hospitalizations and reduced adherence to anticancer treatment, worsening quality of life and survival.
evidence.note: Links cancer-associated sarcopenia (muscle wasting), not malnutrition itself, to morbidity, mortality and quality of life.

claim: The simplified method called malnutrition screening test (MST), which is based on only two parameters, appetite and recent unintentional weight loss, is useful in the assessments of malnutrition in cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.

evidence.quote: MST is a more valid nutritional screening method than MUST and NRS-2002 to predict the loss of lean mass > 5% in oncological patients undergoing radiotherapy treatment. Its routine use is recommended in patients under radiotherapy treatment.
evidence.note: MST judged valid and recommended in radiotherapy patients; validity measured against lean-mass loss. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Two-parameter (appetite, weight loss) composition not stated.

evidence.quote: NRS-2002 demonstrated greater concordance with GLIM criteria than MUST and MST.
evidence.note: In nasopharyngeal radiotherapy patients MST concordance with GLIM was lower than NRS-2002 (kappa 0.378 at admission).

claim: Tumor-induced weight loss occurs frequently in patients with solid tumors of the lung, pancreas, and upper gastrointestinal tract and less often in patients with breast cancer or lower gastrointestinal cancer.

evidence.quote: Tumor subsite is one of the major determinants of malnutrition, with pancreatic, esophageal, and other gastroenteric cancers, head and neck, and lung cancers having the highest prevalence.
evidence.note: Highest malnutrition prevalence in pancreatic, GI and lung cancers; says nothing on breast or lower GI being lower.

claim: Distress is prevalent in approximately one-third of cancer survivors and can be associated with a reduced quality of life.

evidence.quote: One in five CRC survivors showed clinical distress and 86% expressed at least one unmet need.
evidence.note: Reports one in five (not one-third) distress prevalence, in colorectal cancer survivors only; no quality of life link.

evidence.quote: 43.6% of cancer survivors had clinical FCR and 32.1% had severe/pathological FCR.
evidence.note: About one-third have severe fear of recurrence, a specific distress concern, not general distress.

claim: Mood disorders, including anxiety, depression, or post-traumatic stress disorder, are common manifestations of distress.

evidence.quote: Interview-defined depression and anxiety is less common in patients with cancer than previously thought, although some combination of mood disorders occurs in 30-40% of patients in hospital settings without a significant difference between palliative-care and non-palliative-care settings.
evidence.note: Meta-analysis: some mood disorder in 30-40% of hospital cancer patients, though depression and anxiety alone are less common. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Mood disorders as common distress manifestation incl. PTSD; quote says depression/anxiety less common than thought.

evidence.quote: A large percentage found to be classified as depressed (38.2%) and anxious (32.2%) and factors that found to be associated were age, marital status, educational level, stage of cancer from univariate analyses and place of residence, religion, symptoms burden from multivariate analysis (for depression and anxiety).
evidence.note: Breast cancer cohort: 38.2% depressed and 32.2% anxious; PTSD not covered. Strict re-read: the quote does not state PTSD not mentioned; population (cancer patients) not stated.

claim: Studies have shown that using palliative care teams can decrease overall healthcare costs, including improved intensive care unit utilization, decreased emergency department utilization, and reduced inpatient readmission rates.

evidence.quote: Compared with Floor, ED consultations had 8.1 days shorter hospital LOS (3.0 vs. 11.1 days, p < 0.01) with $5,974 lower median direct costs for index hospitalization ($6,211 vs. $12,005, p < 0.01).
evidence.note: ED-embedded palliative care linked to lower hospital costs and stay; ICU use, ED use, readmission not stated.

evidence.quote: Early palliative care consultation ha the potential to provide comfort to patients and families, and decrease costs and length of stay.
evidence.note: States only potential to decrease costs and length of stay; no ICU, ED or readmission data.

claim: In their efforts to define the concept of a "Good Death," researchers narrowed it down to 36 studies that addressed the parameters for good death defined by patients at the end of their life.

evidence.quote: Two thousand six hundred and fifty two titles were identified; after elimination of duplicates, screening, and final selection, 29 relevant publications remained for analysis.
evidence.note: Systematic review of patient views of a good death retained 29 publications, not 36.

claim: Cost sharing policies have increased out-of-pocket expenses for patients, leading to poorer financial well-being, quality of life, psychosocial health, and treatment adherence.

evidence.quote: Regardless of service timing and reconstruction modality, HDHP patients had greater OOP costs compared to LDHP patients, which serves as a good starting point for provider engagement in financial toxicity.
evidence.note: Supports higher out-of-pocket costs under higher cost sharing; not well-being, quality of life or adherence.

evidence.quote: Beneficiaries with higher OOP costs for the more expensive oral cancer drugs were more likely to discontinue or delay drug therapy.
evidence.note: Supports higher out-of-pocket costs linked to poorer adherence; not well-being or quality of life.

claim: Hartstein noted that CMS, which is the biggest payer for cancer care in this country, is prohibited from negotiating prices and interfering with the practice of medicine.

evidence.quote: Starting in 2026, Medicare will be able to negotiate drug prices.
evidence.note: dated: records Medicare gaining negotiation authority (2026), so earlier prohibition is implied but not stated.

claim: There were no significant associations between monthly treatment costs for solid tumours and clinical benefit in all assessed countries.

evidence.quote: There were no significant associations between monthly treatment costs for solid tumours and clinical benefit in all assessed countries, using the ESMO-MCBS (p=0·16 for the USA, p=0·98 for England, p=0·54 for Switzerland, p=0·52 for Germany, and p=0·40 for France)
evidence.note: Matches claim for ESMO-MCBS; the record reports an ASCO-VF association in France (p=0.037).

claim: But nearly 80 percent of the world's children who develop cancer are in resource-poor countries.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, scarce data are available for low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), where nearly 90% of children with cancer reside, suggesting that global survival estimates are substantially worse in these regions.
evidence.note: Gives nearly 90% of children with cancer in LMICs, not 80%; LMICs rather than 'resource-poor'.

claim: Indigenous people are more likely to have cancers that are largely preventable, detectable by screening, and/or have a poor prognosis, such as lung, liver, and cervical cancers.

evidence.quote: Large inequities in cervical cancer currently exist for Indigenous peoples in Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the US, and elimination is not on track for all women in these countries.
evidence.note: one instance: cervical cancer inequity in Indigenous peoples; lung and liver not covered.

evidence.quote: For example, Native Americans have the highest incidence and the slowest decline (less than 1% annually among men and stagnant rates among women) of any group.
evidence.note: one instance: lung cancer incidence highest in Native Americans; other cancers not covered.

claim: Chromosomal instability in early cancer stages is caused by stress on DNA replication.

evidence.quote: This study reveals the dynamics and drivers of APOBEC3 gene expression in preinvasive disease and the exacerbation of cellular diversity by APOBEC3B through DNA replication stress to promote chromosomal instability early in cancer evolution.
evidence.note: Links replication stress to chromosomal instability early in cancer, specifically via APOBEC3B; not stated as the general cause.

claim: Prolonged replication stress can lead to the collapse of replication forks and the formation of DSBs.

evidence.quote: Replication stress triggers complex cellular responses that include cell cycle arrest, replication fork collapse to one-ended DNA double-strand breaks, induction of DNA repair, and programmed cell death after excessive damage.
evidence.note: Replication stress leads to fork collapse into double-strand breaks; 'prolonged' not stated. Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'Prolonged' stress as cause not stated; only that replication stress triggers fork collapse after excessive damage.

claim: Activated p53 induces p21-mediated G1-S checkpoint arrest or triggers apoptosis if damage is irreparable.

evidence.quote: Multifunctional transcription factor that induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis upon binding to its target DNA sequence
evidence.note: p53 induces cell cycle arrest or apoptosis; p21 and G1-S checkpoint not named here.

evidence.quote: One of the activated genes is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases.
evidence.note: An activated gene inhibits CDKs but is not named as p21.

claim: For human pancreatic cancer, the most common causative event is a single missense mutation that is acquired in transforming protein 21 gene (KRAS) that modifies the 12th codon leading ultimately to either valine or aspartate substitution for glycine, finally causing protein activation.

evidence.quote: The KRAS oncogene, present in over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, is most frequently the result of one of three gain-of-function substitution mutations of codon 12 glycine.
evidence.note: Supports codon 12 gain-of-function substitutions in pancreatic cancer; does not name valine or aspartate.

claim: He discussed that both the alleles of a gene need to be lost or mutated for the tumor to develop into a cancer.

evidence.quote: For the development of the disease mutations in both alleles of the gene are required, but an increased risk of developing colorectal cancer in carriers of monoallelic mutations is noted.
evidence.note: Both-allele requirement stated for MutYH-associated polyposis only, not tumor-to-cancer progression in general.

evidence.quote: Thus, loss of the tumour suppressors TP53 and RB1 is obligatory in SCLC.
evidence.note: Bi-allelic tumour suppressor loss is obligatory in small cell lung cancer only.

claim: In particular, studies of the cloned gene have established that Rb is lost or inactivated in many bladder, breast, and lung carcinomas.

evidence.quote: Genomic profiling of SCLC reveals extensive chromosomal rearrangements and a high mutation burden, almost always including functional inactivation of the tumour suppressor genes TP53 and RB1.
evidence.note: one instance: RB1 inactivation in small-cell lung cancer only; bladder and breast not stated.

claim: In total, mutations of p53 may play a role in up to 50% of all cancers, making it the most common target of genetic alterations in human malignancies.

evidence.quote: The tumor suppressor gene TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers and has been a popular area of research in the field of oncology.
evidence.note: Supports TP53 being the most frequently mutated cancer gene; gives no proportion such as 50%.

claim: The active p53 upregulated the expressions of important proteins like cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21, which causes G1-S checkpoint arrest of the cell cycle.

evidence.quote: Involved in p53/TP53 mediated inhibition of cellular proliferation in response to DNA damage.
evidence.note: Links p21 to p53-mediated proliferation inhibition; does not state p53 upregulates its expression.

evidence.quote: Binding to CDK2 leads to CDK2/cyclin E inactivation at the G1-S phase DNA damage checkpoint, thereby arresting cells at the G1-S transition during DNA repair
evidence.note: Supports p21 causing G1-S arrest; upregulation by p53 not stated.

claim: The concept of tumor suppression was further solidified by Alfred Knudson's epidemiological study of retinoblastoma patients that originated the "two-hit hypothesis".

evidence.quote: This year, 2011, marks the forty-year anniversary of the statistical analysis of retinoblastoma that provided the first evidence that tumorigenesis can be initiated by as few as two mutations. This work provided the foundation for the two-hit hypothesis that explained the role of recessive tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) in dominantly inherited cancer susceptibility syndromes.
evidence.note: Retinoblastoma statistical analysis founded the two-hit hypothesis; Knudson is not named.

claim: The DNA damage is perceived by complexes comprising kinases of the ATM/ATR family.

evidence.quote: Serine/threonine protein kinase which activates checkpoint signaling upon genotoxic stresses such as ionizing radiation (IR), ultraviolet light (UV), or DNA replication stalling, thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor
evidence.note: ATR named as DNA damage sensor; ATM and the ATM/ATR family not stated.

claim: Accumulating evidence suggests that chromosome abnormalities represent a genomic signature that is linked to cancer prognosis and reaction to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

evidence.quote: Here, using genomic and transcriptomic studies, we report that LOY correlates with poor prognoses in patients with bladder cancer.
evidence.note: One chromosome abnormality (Y loss) linked to prognosis in bladder cancer; not chromosome abnormalities generally.

evidence.quote: Of note, compared with Y+ tumours, Y- tumours exhibited an increased response to anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade therapy in both mice and patients with cancer.
evidence.note: Y loss linked to immunotherapy response; chemotherapy and general chromosome abnormalities not covered.

claim: Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive disease caused by a lack of BLM helicase enzyme, resulting from a mutation in the BLM gene.

evidence.quote: The Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by growth deficiency, microcephaly and immunodeficiency among others. It is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding DNA helicase RecQ protein on chromosome 15q26.
evidence.note: States autosomal recessive inheritance and causation by mutation in the BLM helicase gene. Strict re-read: the quote does not state BLM gene and lack of BLM helicase not named; quote says mutation in DNA helicase RecQ gene.

claim: Cancer is a multistep, progressive disease, and early chromosomal changes provide the cell with a proliferative advantage.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the Ph translocation might be a first event to immortalize cell proliferation.
evidence.note: One early chromosomal change (Ph translocation in CML) linked to proliferation; general multistep claim not stated.

claim: Chromosome 1 abnormalities are present in most breast carcinomas.

evidence.quote: When data using a different probe from the short arm of chromosome 1 was added, the overall involvement of this region increased to 73%.
evidence.note: 73% of 38 breast cancers showed changes on chromosome 1 short arm; arm-specific, small sample.

evidence.quote: Cytogenetic markers involving the long arm of chromosome 1 are the most frequently observed karyotypic changes seen in breast cancer.
evidence.note: Chromosome 1q changes most frequent in breast cancer; no proportion of carcinomas given.

claim: Numerical chromosome abnormalities, mainly including aneuploidy and chromosome instability, are caused by chromosome segregation errors in mitosis, whereas structural chromosome abnormalities are a consequence of DNA damage and comprise focal/arm-level chromosome gain or loss.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, mitotic errors that result in chromosome mis-segregation are the cause of numerical chromosome instability (n-CIN) and aneuploidy.
evidence.note: Supports the numerical-abnormality half (mitotic segregation errors); structural half given separately.

evidence.quote: A major source of structural chromosome instability (s-CIN) leading to structural chromosome aberrations is "replication stress", a condition in which stalled or slowly progressing replication forks interfere with timely and error-free completion of the S phase.
evidence.note: Structural aberrations attributed to replication stress, not stated as DNA damage.

claim: Philadelphia chromosome is the hallmark of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) along with some other leukemias including acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), chronic neutrophilic leukemia (CNL), and mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL).

evidence.quote: Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
evidence.note: one instance: Ph-positive ALL only; CML, AML, CNL and MPAL not covered.

claim: Theodor Boveri first proposed that chromosomal abnormalities were a common characteristic of tumors over a century ago.

evidence.quote: Failures in accurate chromosome segregation during mitosis can cause numerical aneuploidy, which was hypothesized by Theodor Boveri over a century ago to promote tumorigenesis.
evidence.note: Boveri hypothesis over a century ago concerns aneuploidy promoting tumorigenesis; 'first' and 'common characteristic' not stated.

claim: ATM kinase detects the break and activates repair pathways — homologous recombination (accurate repair using the sister chromatid as template) or non-homologous end joining (faster but error-prone direct rejoining) — to prevent chromosomal breakdown and cancer development.

evidence.quote: Serine/threonine protein kinase which activates checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks (DSBs), apoptosis and genotoxic stresses such as ionizing ultraviolet A light (UVA), thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor
evidence.note: ATM acts as a DNA damage sensor at double strand breaks; HR or NHEJ repair activation not stated.

module: 4.4 DNA Repair Mechanisms and Their Failure in Cancer
claim: Mutations in at least 30 DNA-repair-associated genes have been linked to increased cancer susceptibility or premature aging.

evidence.quote: Mutations in many HR genes lead to cancer predisposition.
evidence.note: one instance: many homologous-recombination repair genes linked to cancer predisposition; no count of 30 and no aging link.

evidence.quote: Similarly, we detected an increase in epigenetic age in fibroblasts isolated from patients with progeroid syndromes associated with mutations in DNA excision repair genes.
evidence.note: one instance: excision repair gene mutations linked to progeroid syndromes; no count given.

module: 4.4 DNA Repair Mechanisms and Their Failure in Cancer
claim: Mutations in genes for proteins responsible for mismatch repairs such as MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 can result in certain cancers such as hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (also known as Lynch Syndrome) and ovarian cancers.

evidence.quote: This gene was identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC).
evidence.note: one instance: MLH1 only linked to hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer; MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 and ovarian cancer not stated.

module: 4.4 DNA Repair Mechanisms and Their Failure in Cancer
claim: The ATM kinase plays an early, pivotal role in the signaling process by detecting DSBs and relaying this information to numerous downstream transducer and effector proteins.

evidence.quote: Serine/threonine protein kinase which activates checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks (DSBs), apoptosis and genotoxic stresses such as ionizing ultraviolet A light (UVA), thereby acting as a DNA damage sensor
evidence.note: ATM described as DNA damage sensor activating checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks.

evidence.quote: Phosphorylates DYRK2, CHEK2, p53/TP53, FBXW7, FANCD2, NFKBIA, BRCA1, CREBBP/CBP, RBBP8/CTIP, FBXO46, MRE11, nibrin (NBN), RAD50, RAD17, PELI1, TERF1, UFL1, RAD9, UBQLN4, UCHL3 and DCLRE1C
evidence.note: Lists many downstream proteins ATM phosphorylates, matching relay to downstream effectors. Strict re-read: the quote does not state ATM detecting DSBs and relaying to transducers; quote only lists phosphorylation substrates.

claim: The list of recurrently mutated cancer genes is relatively short, but there are many rarely mutated genes.

evidence.quote: For most cancer types, this landscape consists of a small number of "mountains" (genes altered in a high percentage of tumors) and a much larger number of "hills" (genes altered infrequently).
evidence.note: Few frequently altered genes versus many infrequently altered genes, matching the claim.

claim: A proto-oncogene on chromosome 9, c-abl, the precursor to the viral oncogene in a mouse leukemia virus, was always found at the junction point in the Philadelphia chromosome, joined to another gene from chromosome 22.

evidence.quote: chromosome 9 9q34.12
evidence.note: ABL1 is located on chromosome 9. Strict re-read: the quote does not state c-abl always at Philadelphia junction, joined to chromosome 22 gene; quote only gives locus 9q34.12.

evidence.quote: This gene has been found fused to a variety of translocation partner genes in various leukemias, most notably the t(9;22) translocation that results in a fusion with the 5' end of the breakpoint cluster region gene (BCR; MIM:151410).
evidence.note: ABL1 fuses with BCR in the t(9;22) translocation; BCR chromosome 22 location is implied by t(9;22). Strict re-read: the quote does not state 'Always found' and c-abl being a precursor of mouse viral oncogene not stated; says BCR fusion in t(9;22).

claim: An avian erythroblastosis virus (AEV) was isolated from a spontaneous erythroleukemia in a chicken in 1908, and soon after, Peyton Rous isolated Rous sarcoma virus from a chicken fibrosarcoma in 1911.

evidence.quote: In 1911, more than a century ago, Peyton Rous described a curious observation, later explained by a virus named for him that led to the discovery of oncogenes
evidence.note: Confirms Rous's 1911 work; chicken fibrosarcoma and the 1908 avian erythroblastosis virus are not stated.

claim: Insertions can occur over a broad range upstream or downstream from many targeted loci, and the proviruses can be in the same transcriptional orientation as the gene or in the opposite orientation.

evidence.quote: These provirus integrations ranged from 217 to 2,584 bp upstream of the TERT transcription initiation site and were all in the opposite transcriptional orientation to TERT.
evidence.note: Example of ALV insertions 217-2,584 bp upstream of TERT, all opposite orientation; downstream and same orientation not stated.

evidence.quote: Extensive surveys of naturally occurring tumors reveal that proviruses integrated on the 3' side of the gene are usually in the same transcriptional orientation, suggesting a model in which the bidirectional viral enhancer acts primarily on the closest promoters.
evidence.note: Proviruses 3' of the gene are usually in the same orientation; supports same-orientation, downstream insertion.

claim: Later identified as a derivative of chromosome 22, this abnormality was designated the Philadelphia chromosome, after its city of discovery.

evidence.quote: This disorder results from the formation of the Philadelphia chromosome that involves a reciprocal translocation that produces a lengthened chromosome 9 and shortened chromosome 22 - the Philadelphia chromosome.
evidence.note: Philadelphia chromosome involves shortened chromosome 22 (and lengthened 9); naming after a city is not stated.

claim: Retroviruses cause a variety of naturally occurring cancers in many animal species and also cause cancers in human beings, including adult t-cell leukemia and hairy cell leukemia.

evidence.quote: Human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) is the only identified oncogenic human retrovirus. HTLV-1 infects approximately 5-10 million people worldwide and is the infectious cause of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL) and several chronic inflammatory diseases, including HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP), dermatitis, and uveitis.
evidence.note: one instance: HTLV-1 causes adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; hairy cell leukemia and animal cancers not stated.

claim: Rous sarcoma virus (RSV) was the first acutely transforming virus shown to have acquired its oncogenicity by the capture of a cellular gene, in this case one called src.

evidence.quote: These transforming sequences have been obtained by avian retroviruses from chicken cellular DNA by recombination.
evidence.note: Avian retroviruses obtained transforming genes from chicken cellular DNA; "first" not stated.

claim: Several overactive growth-promoting genes were identified by isolating and sequencing the DNA fragments that had been transferred to transformed cells.

evidence.quote: Using DNA transfection analysis on NIH 3T3 cells, activated human oncogenes have been isolated from a variety of fresh solid tumours.
evidence.note: Activated oncogenes were isolated from tumours by DNA transfection into NIH 3T3 cells; sequencing not stated. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Isolating and sequencing DNA fragments from transformed cells not stated; only isolating oncogenes by transfection.

evidence.quote: Recently, many cellular oncogenes were identified in human cancerous cells by the DNA transfection method
evidence.note: Many cellular oncogenes were identified in cancer cells by DNA transfection. Strict re-read: the quote does not state Isolating and sequencing of transferred DNA fragments to transformed cells not stated.

claim: Studies revealed that v-src was not truly a viral gene but rather a captured and altered version of a normal cellular gene (c-src or cellular src).

evidence.quote: Since identifying a transmissible agent responsible for tumorigenesis in chickens, the v-Src oncogene, significant progress has been made in determining the functions of its cellular homologue.
evidence.note: v-Src has a cellular homologue c-Src; capture and alteration of the gene is not stated.

claim: The abl protein made from the translocated gene in the Philadelphia chromosome was a fusion protein, encoded mostly by c-abl and partly by the adjacent gene brought in from chromosome 22.

evidence.quote: This gene has been found fused to a variety of translocation partner genes in various leukemias, most notably the t(9;22) translocation that results in a fusion with the 5' end of the breakpoint cluster region gene (BCR; MIM:151410).
evidence.note: ABL1 fuses with BCR via t(9;22); fusion protein and its composition are not described.

claim: The truly revolutionary insight came when it was discovered that viral oncogenes had cellular counterparts in normal DNA.

evidence.quote: However, recent studies have demonstrated that normal eukaryotic cells contain gene sequences which are highly homologous to oncogenes but which do not cause neoplastic transformation.
evidence.note: Normal cells contain sequences highly homologous to oncogenes (proto-oncogenes). Strict re-read: the quote does not state Discovery of cellular counterparts of viral oncogenes not stated.

claim: A significant example of activating point mutations is represented by those affecting the ret protooncogene in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A syndrome (MEN2A).

evidence.quote: This proto-oncogene can undergo oncogenic activation through both cytogenetic rearrangement and activating point mutations.
evidence.note: RET undergoes activating point mutations; MEN2A is only listed as an alias, not tied to them in text.

claim: Ras has been shown to be oncogenically activated by mutations in over 15% of all human tumors, and in some cancers, such as pancreatic carcinoma, the frequency is as high as 90%.

evidence.quote: With a near 100% KRAS mutation frequency, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is considered the most RAS-addicted of all cancers.
evidence.note: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma has near 100% KRAS mutation frequency; overall share across tumors not stated.

evidence.quote: RAS genes (HRAS, KRAS, and NRAS) comprise the most frequently mutated oncogene family in human cancer.
evidence.note: RAS genes are the most frequently mutated oncogene family; no overall percentage.

claim: The K-ras gene is now known to be mutated in a vast number of human cancers, including a quarter of lung cancers, half of colon cancers, and nearly all pancreatic cancers.

evidence.quote: With a near 100% KRAS mutation frequency, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is considered the most RAS-addicted of all cancers.
evidence.note: Supports only pancreatic part: near 100% KRAS mutation in PDAC; lung and colon figures absent.

evidence.quote: 23% of adult pan-cancer samples had KRAS alterations; 88% were mutations
evidence.note: Different scope: 23% of adult pan-cancer samples had KRAS alterations; no lung or colon figures.

claim: The single nucleotide changes that turned a ras proto-oncogene into an oncogene were essentially identical to changes also observed when retroviral ras oncogenes were compared with the proto-oncogenes.

evidence.quote: In the case of the human bladder carcinoma cell lines EJ and T24, this approach has led to the molecular cloning of a transforming gene which is closely related to the rat-derived Harvey sarcoma virus oncogene, v-Ha-ras. A single point mutation, which distinguishes these genes from their normal human homologue (c-Ha-ras1), is thought to be solely responsible for their transforming potential.
evidence.note: A transforming ras gene closely related to v-Ha-ras differs from c-Ha-ras1 by a single point mutation; comparison details limited.

claim: In another childhood tumor, called neuroblastoma, a different member of the myc gene family was often reduplicated ("amplified"), so that many copies of the gene and dangerously large amounts of myc protein were made in the cancer cells.

evidence.quote: Amplification of the MYC family member, MYCN, is found in ∼25% of cases and correlates with high-risk disease and poor prognosis.
evidence.note: MYCN amplification found in about 25% of neuroblastomas; increased protein levels not stated.

module: 5.4 Key Oncogene Families and Their Roles
claim: Proto-oncogenes called Harvey-Ras (H-ras) and Kirsten-Ras (K-ras) are the progenitors of viral oncogenes found in mouse and rat sarcoma viruses.

claim: Ras was first discovered as the hyperactive product of a mutant ras gene that promoted the development of cancer; we now know that about 30% of human tumors have a hyperactive ras mutation.

module: 5.4 Key Oncogene Families and Their Roles
claim: The MYC family represents another major class of oncogenes that function as transcription factors, regulating the expression of genes involved in cell cycle progression, metabolism, and growth.

evidence.quote: Transcription factor that binds DNA in a non-specific manner, yet also specifically recognizes the core sequence 5'-CAC[GA]TG-3' (PubMed:24940000, PubMed:25956029). Activates the transcription of growth-related genes (PubMed:24940000, PubMed:25956029).
evidence.note: MYC is a transcription factor activating growth-related genes; cell cycle and metabolism not stated.

module: 6.1 Discovery and Function of Tumor Suppressor Genes
claim: Gene-mapping studies further indicated that tumor development resulted from loss of normal Rb alleles in the tumor cells, consistent with the function of Rb as a tumor suppressor gene.

evidence.quote: Nonhereditary retinoblastoma is mainly caused by inactivation of both RB1 alleles at a somatic level.
evidence.note: Both RB1 alleles inactivated in tumors; not framed as gene-mapping studies.
